question: Should OpenClaw retain one deterministic pre-processing ack reaction, add a bounded static selection policy, or support model-driven contextual selection?
rationale: The request introduces new user-facing configuration and changes acknowledgment timing/behavior across channels; source evidence does not establish one semantics as the existing contract.

options.title: Retain one configured reaction
options.body: Keep the existing low-latency singular contract and leave varied reactions to explicit message-tool behavior.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded static pool
options.body: Add an opt-in deterministic or random pool only after defining cross-channel validation, fallback, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Sponsor contextual model selection
options.body: Design an explicit pre-ack model/strategy contract with a latency budget and failure fallback before implementation.

recommendation.title: Retain one configured reaction
recommendation.body: Keep the existing low-latency singular contract and leave varied reactions to explicit message-tool behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion already records this person as the visible reviewer holding the feature for a product decision.
